enums.name: QueryType

values.name: Simple
values.doc: Uses the simple query syntax for searches. Search text is interpreted using a simple query language that allows for symbols such as +, * and "". Queries are evaluated across all searchable fields by default, unless the searchFields parameter is specified.

values.name: Full
values.doc: Uses the full Lucene query syntax for searches. Search text is interpreted using the Lucene query language which allows field-specific and weighted searches, as well as other advanced features.

values.name: Semantic
values.doc: Best suited for queries expressed in natural language as opposed to keywords. Improves precision of search results by re-ranking the top search results using a ranking model trained on the Web corpus.

enums.doc: Specifies the syntax of the search query. The default is 'simple'. Use 'full' if your query uses the Lucene query syntax and 'semantic' if query syntax is not needed.

enums.name: ScoringStatistics

values.name: Local
values.doc: The scoring statistics will be calculated locally for lower latency.

values.name: Global
values.doc: The scoring statistics will be calculated globally for more consistent scoring.

enums.doc: A value that specifies whether we want to calculate scoring statistics (such as document frequency) globally for more consistent scoring, or locally, for lower latency. The default is 'local'. Use 'global' to aggregate scoring statistics globally before scoring. Using global scoring statistics can increase latency of search queries.

enums.name: QueryDebugMode

values.name: Disabled
values.doc: No query debugging information will be returned.

values.name: Semantic
values.doc: Allows the user to further explore their reranked results.

values.name: Vector
values.doc: Allows the user to further explore their hybrid and vector query results.

values.name: QueryRewrites
values.doc: Allows the user to explore the list of query rewrites generated for their search request.

values.name: InnerHits
values.doc: Allows the user to retrieve scoring information regarding vectors matched within a collection of complex types.

enums.doc: Enables a debugging tool that can be used to further explore your search results. You can enable multiple debug modes simultaneously by separating them with a | character, for example: semantic|queryRewrites.

enums.name: SearchMode

values.name: Any
values.doc: Any of the search terms must be matched in order to count the document as a match.

values.name: All
values.doc: All of the search terms must be matched in order to count the document as a match.

enums.doc: Specifies whether any or all of the search terms must be matched in order to count the document as a match.

enums.name: QueryLanguage

values.name: EnUs
values.doc: Query language value for English (United States).

values.name: EnGb
values.doc: Query language value for English (Great Britain).

values.name: CsCz
values.doc: Query language value for Czech (Czech Republic).

values.name: ArSa
values.doc: Query language value for Arabic (Saudi Arabia).

values.name: HrBa
values.doc: Query language value for Croatian (Bosnia and Herzegovina).

values.name: MsBn
values.doc: Query language value for Malay (Brunei Darussalam).

values.name: ViVn
values.doc: Query language value for Vietnamese (Viet Nam).

values.name: SrBa
values.doc: Query language value for Serbian (Bosnia and Herzegovina).

enums.doc: The language of the query.

enums.name: QuerySpellerType

values.name: Lexicon
values.doc: Speller corrects individual query terms using a static lexicon for the language specified by the queryLanguage parameter.

enums.doc: Improve search recall by spell-correcting individual search query terms.

enums.name: SemanticErrorMode

values.name: Partial
values.doc: If the semantic processing fails, partial results still return. The definition of partial results depends on what semantic step failed and what was the reason for failure.

values.name: Fail
values.doc: If there is an exception during the semantic processing step, the query will fail and return the appropriate HTTP code depending on the error.

enums.doc: Allows the user to choose whether a semantic call should fail completely, or to return partial results.

enums.name: QueryAnswerType

values.name: None
values.doc: Do not return answers for the query.

values.name: Extractive
values.doc: Extracts answer candidates from the contents of the documents returned in response to a query expressed as a question in natural language.

enums.doc: This parameter is only valid if the query type is `semantic`. If set, the query returns answers extracted from key passages in the highest ranked documents. The number of answers returned can be configured by appending the pipe character `|` followed by the `count-<number of answers>` option after the answers parameter value, such as `extractive|count-3`. Default count is 1. The confidence threshold can be configured by appending the pipe character `|` followed by the `threshold-<confidence threshold>` option after the answers parameter value, such as `extractive|threshold-0.9`. Default threshold is 0.7. The maximum character length of answers can be configured by appending the pipe character '|' followed by the 'count-<number of maximum character length>', such as 'extractive|maxcharlength-600'.

enums.name: QueryCaptionType

values.name: None
values.doc: Do not return captions for the query.

values.name: Extractive
values.doc: Extracts captions from the matching documents that contain passages relevant to the search query.

enums.doc: This parameter is only valid if the query type is `semantic`. If set, the query returns captions extracted from key passages in the highest ranked documents. When Captions is set to `extractive`, highlighting is enabled by default, and can be configured by appending the pipe character `|` followed by the `highlight-<true/false>` option, such as `extractive|highlight-true`. Defaults to `None`. The maximum character length of captions can be configured by appending the pipe character '|' followed by the 'count-<number of maximum character length>', such as 'extractive|maxcharlength-600'.

enums.name: QueryRewritesType

values.name: None
values.doc: Do not generate additional query rewrites for this query.

values.name: Generative
values.doc: Generate alternative query terms to increase the recall of a search request.

enums.doc: This parameter is only valid if the query type is `semantic`. When QueryRewrites is set to `generative`, the query terms are sent to a generate model which will produce 10 (default) rewrites to help increase the recall of the request. The requested count can be configured by appending the pipe character `|` followed by the `count-<number of rewrites>` option, such as `generative|count-3`. Defaults to `None`.

enums.name: VectorThresholdKind

values.name: VectorSimilarity
values.doc: The results of the vector query will be filtered based on the vector similarity metric. Note this is the canonical definition of similarity metric, not the 'distance' version. The threshold direction (larger or smaller) will be chosen automatically according to the metric used by the field.

values.name: SearchScore
values.doc: The results of the vector query will filter based on the '@search.score' value. Note this is the @search.score returned as part of the search response. The threshold direction will be chosen for higher @search.score.

enums.doc: The kind of threshold used to filter vector queries.

enums.name: VectorQueryKind

values.name: Vector
values.doc: Vector query where a raw vector value is provided.

values.name: Text
values.doc: Vector query where a text value that needs to be vectorized is provided.

values.name: ImageUrl
values.doc: Vector query where an url that represents an image value that needs to be vectorized is provided.

values.name: ImageBinary
values.doc: Vector query where a base 64 encoded binary of an image that needs to be vectorized is provided.

enums.doc: The kind of vector query being performed.

enums.name: VectorFilterMode

values.name: PostFilter
values.doc: The filter will be applied after the candidate set of vector results is returned. Depending on the filter selectivity, this can result in fewer results than requested by the parameter 'k'.

values.name: PreFilter
values.doc: The filter will be applied before the search query.

values.name: StrictPostFilter
values.doc: The filter will be applied after the global top-k candidate set of vector results is returned. This will result in fewer results than requested by the parameter 'k'.

enums.doc: Determines whether or not filters are applied before or after the vector search is performed.

enums.name: HybridCountAndFacetMode

values.name: CountRetrievableResults
values.doc: Only include documents that were matched within the 'maxTextRecallSize' retrieval window when computing 'count' and 'facets'.

values.name: CountAllResults
values.doc: Include all documents that were matched by the search query when computing 'count' and 'facets', regardless of whether or not those documents are within the 'maxTextRecallSize' retrieval window.

enums.doc: Determines whether the count and facets should includes all documents that matched the search query, or only the documents that are retrieved within the 'maxTextRecallSize' window. The default value is 'countAllResults'.

enums.name: SemanticFieldState

values.name: Used
values.doc: The field was fully used for semantic enrichment.

values.name: Unused
values.doc: The field was not used for semantic enrichment.

values.name: Partial
values.doc: The field was partially used for semantic enrichment.

enums.doc: The way the field was used for the semantic enrichment process.

enums.name: SemanticErrorReason

values.name: MaxWaitExceeded
values.doc: If `semanticMaxWaitInMilliseconds` was set and the semantic processing duration exceeded that value. Only the base results were returned.

values.name: CapacityOverloaded
values.doc: The request was throttled. Only the base results were returned.

values.name: Transient
values.doc: At least one step of the semantic process failed.

enums.doc: Reason that a partial response was returned for a semantic ranking request.

enums.name: SemanticSearchResultsType

values.name: BaseResults
values.doc: Results without any semantic enrichment or reranking.

values.name: RerankedResults
values.doc: Results have been reranked with the reranker model and will include semantic captions. They will not include any answers, answers highlights or caption highlights.

enums.doc: Type of partial response that was returned for a semantic ranking request.

enums.name: SemanticQueryRewritesResultType

values.name: OriginalQueryOnly
values.doc: Query rewrites were not successfully generated for this request. Only the original query was used to retrieve the results.

enums.doc: Type of query rewrite that was used for this request.

enums.name: IndexActionType

values.name: Upload
values.doc: Inserts the document into the index if it is new and updates it if it exists. All fields are replaced in the update case.

values.name: Merge
values.doc: Merges the specified field values with an existing document. If the document does not exist, the merge will fail. Any field you specify in a merge will replace the existing field in the document. This also applies to collections of primitive and complex types.

values.name: MergeOrUpload
values.doc: Behaves like merge if a document with the given key already exists in the index. If the document does not exist, it behaves like upload with a new document.

values.name: Delete
values.doc: Removes the specified document from the index. Any field you specify in a delete operation other than the key field will be ignored. If you want to remove an individual field from a document, use merge instead and set the field explicitly to null.

enums.doc: The operation to perform on a document in an indexing batch.

enums.name: AutocompleteMode

values.name: OneTerm
values.doc: Only one term is suggested. If the query has two terms, only the last term is completed. For example, if the input is 'washington medic', the suggested terms could include 'medicaid', 'medicare', and 'medicine'.

values.name: TwoTerms
values.doc: Matching two-term phrases in the index will be suggested. For example, if the input is 'medic', the suggested terms could include 'medicare coverage' and 'medical assistant'.

values.name: OneTermWithContext
values.doc: Completes the last term in a query with two or more terms, where the last two terms are a phrase that exists in the index. For example, if the input is 'washington medic', the suggested terms could include 'washington medicaid' and 'washington medical'.

enums.doc: Specifies the mode for Autocomplete. The default is 'oneTerm'. Use 'twoTerms' to get shingles and 'oneTermWithContext' to use the current context in producing autocomplete terms.

enums.name: SearchFieldDataType

values.name: String
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a string.

values.name: Int32
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a 32-bit signed integer.

values.name: Int64
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a 64-bit signed integer.

values.name: Double
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains an IEEE double-precision floating point number.

values.name: Boolean
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a Boolean value (true or false).

values.name: DateTimeOffset
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a date/time value, including timezone information.

values.name: GeographyPoint
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a geo-location in terms of longitude and latitude.

values.name: Complex
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains one or more complex objects that in turn have sub-fields of other types.

values.name: Single
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a single-precision floating point number. This is only valid when used with Collection(Edm.Single).

values.name: Half
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a half-precision floating point number. This is only valid when used with Collection(Edm.Half).

values.name: Int16
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a 16-bit signed integer. This is only valid when used with Collection(Edm.Int16).

values.name: SByte
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a 8-bit signed integer. This is only valid when used with Collection(Edm.SByte).

values.name: Byte
values.doc: Indicates that a field contains a 8-bit unsigned integer. This is only valid when used with Collection(Edm.Byte).

enums.doc: Defines the data type of a field in a search index.

enums.name: PermissionFilter

values.name: UserIds
values.doc: Field represents user IDs that should be used to filter document access on queries.

values.name: GroupIds
values.doc: Field represents group IDs that should be used to filter document access on queries.

values.name: RbacScope
values.doc: Field represents an RBAC scope that should be used to filter document access on queries.

enums.doc: A value indicating whether the field should be used as a permission filter.

enums.name: LexicalAnalyzerName

values.name: StandardAsciiFoldingLucene
values.doc: Standard ASCII Folding Lucene analyzer. See https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/searchservice/Custom-analyzers-in-Azure-Search#Analyzers

values.name: Keyword
values.doc: Treats the entire content of a field as a single token. This is useful for data like zip codes, ids, and some product names. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/KeywordAnalyzer.html

values.name: Pattern
values.doc: Flexibly separates text into terms via a regular expression pattern. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/PatternAnalyzer.html

values.name: Simple
values.doc: Divides text at non-letters and converts them to lower case. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/SimpleAnalyzer.html

values.name: Stop
values.doc: Divides text at non-letters; Applies the lowercase and stopword token filters. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/StopAnalyzer.html

values.name: Whitespace
values.doc: An analyzer that uses the whitespace tokenizer. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/WhitespaceAnalyzer.html

enums.doc: Defines the names of all text analyzers supported by the search engine.

enums.name: LexicalNormalizerName

values.name: AsciiFolding
values.doc: Converts alphabetic, numeric, and symbolic Unicode characters which are not in the first 127 ASCII characters (the "Basic Latin" Unicode block) into their ASCII equivalents, if such equivalents exist. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/ASCIIFoldingFilter.html

values.name: Elision
values.doc: Removes elisions. For example, "l'avion" (the plane) will be converted to "avion" (plane). See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/util/ElisionFilter.html

values.name: Lowercase
values.doc: Normalizes token text to lowercase. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/6_6_1/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/LowerCaseFilter.html

values.name: Standard
values.doc: Standard normalizer, which consists of lowercase and asciifolding. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/reverse/ReverseStringFilter.html

values.name: Uppercase
values.doc: Normalizes token text to uppercase. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/6_6_1/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/UpperCaseFilter.html

enums.doc: Defines the names of all text normalizers supported by the search engine.

enums.name: VectorEncodingFormat

values.name: PackedBit
values.doc: Encoding format representing bits packed into a wider data type.

enums.doc: The encoding format for interpreting vector field contents.

enums.name: ScoringFunctionInterpolation

values.name: Linear
values.doc: Boosts scores by a linearly decreasing amount. This is the default interpolation for scoring functions.

values.name: Constant
values.doc: Boosts scores by a constant factor.

values.name: Quadratic
values.doc: Boosts scores by an amount that decreases quadratically. Boosts decrease slowly for higher scores, and more quickly as the scores decrease. This interpolation option is not allowed in tag scoring functions.

values.name: Logarithmic
values.doc: Boosts scores by an amount that decreases logarithmically. Boosts decrease quickly for higher scores, and more slowly as the scores decrease. This interpolation option is not allowed in tag scoring functions.

enums.doc: Defines the function used to interpolate score boosting across a range of documents.

enums.name: ScoringFunctionAggregation

values.name: Sum
values.doc: Boost scores by the sum of all scoring function results.

values.name: Average
values.doc: Boost scores by the average of all scoring function results.

values.name: Minimum
values.doc: Boost scores by the minimum of all scoring function results.

values.name: Maximum
values.doc: Boost scores by the maximum of all scoring function results.

values.name: FirstMatching
values.doc: Boost scores using the first applicable scoring function in the scoring profile.

values.name: Product
values.doc: Boost scores by the product of all scoring function results.

enums.doc: Defines the aggregation function used to combine the results of all the scoring functions in a scoring profile.

enums.name: LexicalTokenizerName

values.name: Classic
values.doc: Grammar-based tokenizer that is suitable for processing most European-language documents. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/standard/ClassicTokenizer.html

values.name: EdgeNGram
values.doc: Tokenizes the input from an edge into n-grams of the given size(s). See https://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ngram/EdgeNGramTokenizer.html

values.name: Keyword
values.doc: Emits the entire input as a single token. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/KeywordTokenizer.html

values.name: Lowercase
values.doc: Divides text at non-letters and converts them to lower case. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/LowerCaseTokenizer.html

values.name: MicrosoftLanguageStemmingTokenizer
values.doc: Divides text using language-specific rules and reduces words to their base forms.

values.name: NGram
values.doc: Tokenizes the input into n-grams of the given size(s). See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ngram/NGramTokenizer.html

values.name: Pattern
values.doc: Tokenizer that uses regex pattern matching to construct distinct tokens. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/pattern/PatternTokenizer.html

values.name: Standard
values.doc: Standard Lucene analyzer; Composed of the standard tokenizer, lowercase filter and stop filter. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/standard/StandardTokenizer.html

values.name: UaxUrlEmail
values.doc: Tokenizes urls and emails as one token. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/standard/UAX29URLEmailTokenizer.html

enums.doc: Defines the names of all tokenizers supported by the search engine.

enums.name: TokenFilterName

values.name: ArabicNormalization
values.doc: A token filter that applies the Arabic normalizer to normalize the orthography. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ar/ArabicNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: Apostrophe
values.doc: Strips all characters after an apostrophe (including the apostrophe itself). See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/tr/ApostropheFilter.html

values.name: AsciiFolding
values.doc: Converts alphabetic, numeric, and symbolic Unicode characters which are not in the first 127 ASCII characters (the "Basic Latin" Unicode block) into their ASCII equivalents, if such equivalents exist. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/ASCIIFoldingFilter.html

values.name: CjkBigram
values.doc: Forms bigrams of CJK terms that are generated from the standard tokenizer. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/cjk/CJKBigramFilter.html

values.name: CjkWidth
values.doc: Normalizes CJK width differences. Folds full-width ASCII variants into the equivalent basic Latin, and half-width Katakana variants into the equivalent Kana. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/cjk/CJKWidthFilter.html

values.name: Classic
values.doc: Removes English possessives, and dots from acronyms. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/standard/ClassicFilter.html

values.name: CommonGram
values.doc: Construct bigrams for frequently occurring terms while indexing. Single terms are still indexed too, with bigrams overlaid. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/commongrams/CommonGramsFilter.html

values.name: EdgeNGram
values.doc: Generates n-grams of the given size(s) starting from the front or the back of an input token. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ngram/EdgeNGramTokenFilter.html

values.name: Elision
values.doc: Removes elisions. For example, "l'avion" (the plane) will be converted to "avion" (plane). See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/util/ElisionFilter.html

values.name: GermanNormalization
values.doc: Normalizes German characters according to the heuristics of the German2 snowball algorithm. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/de/GermanNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: HindiNormalization
values.doc: Normalizes text in Hindi to remove some differences in spelling variations. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/hi/HindiNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: IndicNormalization
values.doc: Normalizes the Unicode representation of text in Indian languages. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/in/IndicNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: KeywordRepeat
values.doc: Emits each incoming token twice, once as keyword and once as non-keyword. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/KeywordRepeatFilter.html

values.name: KStem
values.doc: A high-performance kstem filter for English. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/en/KStemFilter.html

values.name: Length
values.doc: Removes words that are too long or too short. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/LengthFilter.html

values.name: Limit
values.doc: Limits the number of tokens while indexing. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/LimitTokenCountFilter.html

values.name: Lowercase
values.doc: Normalizes token text to lower case. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/6_6_1/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/LowerCaseFilter.html

values.name: NGram
values.doc: Generates n-grams of the given size(s). See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ngram/NGramTokenFilter.html

values.name: Phonetic
values.doc: Create tokens for phonetic matches. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-phonetic/org/apache/lucene/analysis/phonetic/package-tree.html

values.name: PorterStem
values.doc: Uses the Porter stemming algorithm to transform the token stream. See http://tartarus.org/~martin/PorterStemmer

values.name: ScandinavianNormalization
values.doc: Normalizes use of the interchangeable Scandinavian characters. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/ScandinavianNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: ScandinavianFoldingNormalization
values.doc: Folds Scandinavian characters Ã¥Ã…Ã¤Ã¦Ã„Ã†->a and Ã¶Ã–Ã¸Ã˜->o. It also discriminates against use of double vowels aa, ae, ao, oe and oo, leaving just the first one. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/ScandinavianFoldingFilter.html

values.name: Shingle
values.doc: Creates combinations of tokens as a single token. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/shingle/ShingleFilter.html

values.name: Snowball
values.doc: A filter that stems words using a Snowball-generated stemmer. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/snowball/SnowballFilter.html

values.name: SoraniNormalization
values.doc: Normalizes the Unicode representation of Sorani text. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ckb/SoraniNormalizationFilter.html

values.name: Stopwords
values.doc: Removes stop words from a token stream. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/StopFilter.html

values.name: Trim
values.doc: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from tokens. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/TrimFilter.html

values.name: Truncate
values.doc: Truncates the terms to a specific length. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/TruncateTokenFilter.html

values.name: Unique
values.doc: Filters out tokens with same text as the previous token. See http://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/miscellaneous/RemoveDuplicatesTokenFilter.html

values.name: Uppercase
values.doc: Normalizes token text to upper case. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/6_6_1/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/core/UpperCaseFilter.html

values.name: WordDelimiter
values.doc: Splits words into subwords and performs optional transformations on subword groups.

enums.doc: Defines the names of all token filters supported by the search engine.

enums.name: CharFilterName

values.name: HtmlStrip
values.doc: A character filter that attempts to strip out HTML constructs. See https://lucene.apache.org/core/4_10_3/analyzers-common/org/apache/lucene/analysis/charfilter/HTMLStripCharFilter.html

enums.doc: Defines the names of all character filters supported by the search engine.

enums.name: RegexFlag

values.name: Comments
values.doc: Permits whitespace and comments in the pattern.

values.name: Literal
values.doc: Enables literal parsing of the pattern.

enums.doc: Defines a regular expression flag that can be used in the pattern analyzer and pattern tokenizer.

enums.name: VectorSearchAlgorithmKind

values.name: Hnsw
values.doc: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World), a type of approximate nearest neighbors algorithm.

values.name: ExhaustiveKnn
values.doc: Exhaustive KNN algorithm which will perform brute-force search.

enums.doc: The algorithm used for indexing and querying.

enums.name: VectorSearchAlgorithmMetric

values.name: Cosine
values.doc: Measures the angle between vectors to quantify their similarity, disregarding magnitude. The smaller the angle, the closer the similarity.

values.name: Euclidean
values.doc: Computes the straight-line distance between vectors in a multi-dimensional space. The smaller the distance, the closer the similarity.

values.name: DotProduct
values.doc: Calculates the sum of element-wise products to gauge alignment and magnitude similarity. The larger and more positive, the closer the similarity.

values.name: Hamming
values.doc: Only applicable to bit-packed binary data types. Determines dissimilarity by counting differing positions in binary vectors. The fewer differences, the closer the similarity.

enums.doc: The similarity metric to use for vector comparisons. It is recommended to choose the same similarity metric as the embedding model was trained on.

enums.name: VectorSearchCompressionRescoreStorageMethod

values.name: PreserveOriginals
values.doc: This option preserves the original full-precision vectors. Choose this option for maximum flexibility and highest quality of compressed search results. This consumes more storage but allows for rescoring and oversampling.

values.name: DiscardOriginals
values.doc: This option discards the original full-precision vectors. Choose this option for maximum storage savings. Since this option does not allow for rescoring and oversampling, it will often cause slight to moderate reductions in quality.

enums.doc: The storage method for the original full-precision vectors used for rescoring and internal index operations.

enums.name: VectorSearchCompressionKind

values.name: ScalarQuantization
values.doc: Scalar Quantization, a type of compression method. In scalar quantization, the original vectors values are compressed to a narrower type by discretizing and representing each component of a vector using a reduced set of quantized values, thereby reducing the overall data size.

values.name: BinaryQuantization
values.doc: Binary Quantization, a type of compression method. In binary quantization, the original vectors values are compressed to the narrower binary type by discretizing and representing each component of a vector using binary values, thereby reducing the overall data size.

enums.doc: The compression method used for indexing and querying.

enums.name: VectorSearchCompressionTarget
enums.doc: The quantized data type of compressed vector values.

This applies to embedded image content in a .PDF or other application, or image files such as .jpg and .png, in Azure blobs.

enums.name: BlobIndexerImageAction

values.name: None
values.doc: Ignores embedded images or image files in the data set.  This is the default.

values.name: GenerateNormalizedImages
values.doc: Extracts text from images (for example, the word "STOP" from a traffic stop sign), and embeds it into the content field.  This action requires that "dataToExtract" is set to "contentAndMetadata".  A normalized image refers to additional processing resulting in uniform image output, sized and rotated to promote consistent rendering when you include images in visual search results. This information is generated for each image when you use this option.

values.name: GenerateNormalizedImagePerPage
values.doc: Extracts text from images (for example, the word "STOP" from a traffic stop sign), and embeds it into the content field, but treats PDF files differently in that each page will be rendered as an image and normalized accordingly, instead of extracting embedded images.  Non-PDF file types will be treated the same as if "generateNormalizedImages" was set.

values.doc: May produce better and more readable text extraction from PDF files that have rotated text within them.  Note that there may be a small performance speed impact when this parameter is used.  This parameter only applies to PDF files, and only to PDFs with embedded text.  If the rotated text appears within an embedded image in the PDF, this parameter does not apply.

models.doc: Response containing search results from an index.

properties.name: count
properties.doc: The total count of results found by the search operation, or null if the count was not requested. If present, the count may be greater than the number of results in this response. This can happen if you use the $top or $skip parameters, or if the query can't return all the requested documents in a single response.

properties.name: coverage
properties.doc: A value indicating the percentage of the index that was included in the query, or null if minimumCoverage was not specified in the request.

properties.name: facets
properties.doc: The facet query results for the search operation, organized as a collection of buckets for each faceted field; null if the query did not include any facet expressions.

valueType.name: FacetResult
valueType.doc: A single bucket of a facet query result. Reports the number of documents with a field value falling within a particular range or having a particular value or interval.

properties.name: count
properties.doc: The approximate count of documents falling within the bucket described by this facet.

properties.name: avg
properties.doc: The resulting total avg for the facet when a avg metric is requested.

properties.name: min
properties.doc: The resulting total min for the facet when a min metric is requested.

properties.name: max
properties.doc: The resulting total max for the facet when a max metric is requested.

properties.name: sum
properties.doc: The resulting total sum for the facet when a sum metric is requested.

properties.name: cardinality
properties.doc: The resulting total cardinality for the facet when a cardinality metric is requested.

properties.name: facets
properties.doc: The nested facet query results for the search operation, organized as a collection of buckets for each faceted field; null if the query did not contain any nested facets.

properties.name: answers
properties.doc: The answers query results for the search operation; null if the answers query parameter was not specified or set to 'none'.

valueType.name: QueryAnswerResult
valueType.doc: An answer is a text passage extracted from the contents of the most relevant documents that matched the query. Answers are extracted from the top search results. Answer candidates are scored and the top answers are selected.

properties.name: score
properties.doc: The score value represents how relevant the answer is to the query relative to other answers returned for the query.

properties.name: key
properties.doc: The key of the document the answer was extracted from.

properties.name: text
properties.doc: The text passage extracted from the document contents as the answer.

properties.name: highlights
properties.doc: Same text passage as in the Text property with highlighted text phrases most relevant to the query.

properties.name: debugInfo
properties.doc: Debug information that applies to the search results as a whole.

type.name: DebugInfo
type.doc: Contains debugging information that can be used to further explore your search results.

properties.name: queryRewrites
properties.doc: Contains debugging information specific to query rewrites.

type.name: QueryRewritesDebugInfo
type.doc: Contains debugging information specific to query rewrites.

properties.name: text
properties.doc: List of query rewrites generated for the text query.

type.name: QueryRewritesValuesDebugInfo
type.doc: Contains debugging information specific to query rewrites.

properties.name: inputQuery
properties.doc: The input text to the generative query rewriting model. There may be cases where the user query and the input to the generative model are not identical.

properties.name: rewrites
properties.doc: List of query rewrites.

properties.name: vectors
properties.doc: List of query rewrites generated for the vectorizable text queries.

properties.name: nextPageParameters
properties.doc: Continuation JSON payload returned when the query can't return all the requested results in a single response. You can use this JSON along with

type.name: SearchRequest
type.doc: Parameters for filtering, sorting, faceting, paging, and other search query behaviors.

properties.name: includeTotalCount
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether to fetch the total count of results. Default is false. Setting this value to true may have a performance impact. Note that the count returned is an approximation.

properties.name: facets
properties.doc: The list of facet expressions to apply to the search query. Each facet expression contains a field name, optionally followed by a comma-separated list of name:value pairs.

properties.name: filter
properties.doc: The OData $filter expression to apply to the search query.

properties.name: highlightFields
properties.doc: The comma-separated list of field names to use for hit highlights. Only searchable fields can be used for hit highlighting.

properties.name: highlightPostTag
properties.doc: A string tag that is appended to hit highlights. Must be set with highlightPreTag. Default is </em>.

properties.name: highlightPreTag
properties.doc: A string tag that is prepended to hit highlights. Must be set with highlightPostTag. Default is <em>.

properties.name: minimumCoverage
properties.doc: A number between 0 and 100 indicating the percentage of the index that must be covered by a search query in order for the query to be reported as a success. This parameter can be useful for ensuring search availability even for services with only one replica. The default is 100.

properties.name: orderBy
properties.doc: The comma-separated list of OData $orderby expressions by which to sort the results. Each expression can be either a field name or a call to either the geo.distance() or the search.score() functions. Each expression can be followed by asc to indicate ascending, or desc to indicate descending. The default is ascending order. Ties will be broken by the match scores of documents. If no $orderby is specified, the default sort order is descending by document match score. There can be at most 32 $orderby clauses.

properties.name: queryType
properties.doc: A value that specifies the syntax of the search query. The default is 'simple'. Use 'full' if your query uses the Lucene query syntax.

properties.name: scoringStatistics
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether we want to calculate scoring statistics (such as document frequency) globally for more consistent scoring, or locally, for lower latency. The default is 'local'. Use 'global' to aggregate scoring statistics globally before scoring. Using global scoring statistics can increase latency of search queries.

properties.name: sessionId
properties.doc: A value to be used to create a sticky session, which can help getting more consistent results. As long as the same sessionId is used, a best-effort attempt will be made to target the same replica set. Be wary that reusing the same sessionID values repeatedly can interfere with the load balancing of the requests across replicas and adversely affect the performance of the search service. The value used as sessionId cannot start with a '_' character.

properties.name: scoringParameters
properties.doc: The list of parameter values to be used in scoring functions (for example, referencePointParameter) using the format name-values. For example, if the scoring profile defines a function with a parameter called 'mylocation' the parameter string would be "mylocation--122.2,44.8" (without the quotes).

properties.name: scoringProfile
properties.doc: The name of a scoring profile to evaluate match scores for matching documents in order to sort the results.

properties.name: debug
properties.doc: Enables a debugging tool that can be used to further explore your reranked results.

properties.name: searchText
properties.doc: A full-text search query expression; Use "*" or omit this parameter to match all documents.

properties.name: searchFields
properties.doc: The comma-separated list of field names to which to scope the full-text search. When using fielded search (fieldName:searchExpression) in a full Lucene query, the field names of each fielded search expression take precedence over any field names listed in this parameter.

properties.name: searchMode
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether any or all of the search terms must be matched in order to count the document as a match.

properties.name: queryLanguage
properties.doc: A value that specifies the language of the search query.

properties.name: querySpeller
properties.doc: A value that specifies the type of the speller to use to spell-correct individual search query terms.

properties.name: select
properties.doc: The comma-separated list of fields to retrieve. If unspecified, all fields marked as retrievable in the schema are included.

properties.name: skip
properties.doc: The number of search results to skip. This value cannot be greater than 100,000. If you need to scan documents in sequence, but cannot use skip due to this limitation, consider using orderby on a totally-ordered key and filter with a range query instead.

properties.name: top
properties.doc: The number of search results to retrieve. This can be used in conjunction with $skip to implement client-side paging of search results. If results are truncated due to server-side paging, the response will include a continuation token that can be used to issue another Search request for the next page of results.

properties.name: semanticConfigurationName
properties.doc: The name of a semantic configuration that will be used when processing documents for queries of type semantic.

properties.name: semanticErrorHandling
properties.doc: Allows the user to choose whether a semantic call should fail completely (default / current behavior), or to return partial results.

properties.name: semanticMaxWaitInMilliseconds
properties.doc: Allows the user to set an upper bound on the amount of time it takes for semantic enrichment to finish processing before the request fails.

properties.name: semanticQuery
properties.doc: Allows setting a separate search query that will be solely used for semantic reranking, semantic captions and semantic answers. Is useful for scenarios where there is a need to use different queries between the base retrieval and ranking phase, and the L2 semantic phase.

properties.name: answers
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether answers should be returned as part of the search response.

properties.name: captions
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether captions should be returned as part of the search response.

properties.name: queryRewrites
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether query rewrites should be generated to augment the search query.

properties.name: semanticFields
properties.doc: The comma-separated list of field names used for semantic ranking.

properties.name: vectorQueries
properties.doc: The query parameters for vector and hybrid search queries.

valueType.name: VectorQuery
valueType.doc: The query parameters for vector and hybrid search queries.

properties.name: kNearestNeighborsCount
properties.doc: Number of nearest neighbors to return as top hits.

properties.name: fields
properties.doc: Vector Fields of type Collection(Edm.Single) to be included in the vector searched.

properties.name: exhaustive
properties.doc: When true, triggers an exhaustive k-nearest neighbor search across all vectors within the vector index. Useful for scenarios where exact matches are critical, such as determining ground truth values.

properties.name: oversampling
properties.doc: Oversampling factor. Minimum value is 1. It overrides the 'defaultOversampling' parameter configured in the index definition. It can be set only when 'rerankWithOriginalVectors' is true. This parameter is only permitted when a compression method is used on the underlying vector field.

properties.name: weight
properties.doc: Relative weight of the vector query when compared to other vector query and/or the text query within the same search request. This value is used when combining the results of multiple ranking lists produced by the different vector queries and/or the results retrieved through the text query. The higher the weight, the higher the documents that matched that query will be in the final ranking. Default is 1.0 and the value needs to be a positive number larger than zero.

properties.name: threshold
properties.doc: The threshold used for vector queries. Note this can only be set if all 'fields' use the same similarity metric.

properties.doc: The comma-separated list of OData $orderby expressions by which to sort the results. Each expression can be either a field name or a call to either the geo.distance() or the search.score() functions. Each expression can be followed by asc to indicate ascending, or desc to indicate descending. The default is ascending order. Ties will be broken by the match scores of documents. If no $orderby is specified, the default sort order is descending by document match score. There can be at most 32 $orderby clauses.

properties.name: queryType
properties.doc: A value that specifies the syntax of the search query. The default is 'simple'. Use 'full' if your query uses the Lucene query syntax.

properties.name: scoringStatistics
properties.doc: A value that specifies whether we want to calculate scoring statistics (such as document frequency) globally for more consistent scoring, or locally, for lower latency. The default is 'local'. Use 'global' to aggregate scoring statistics globally before scoring. Using global scoring statistics can increase latency of search queries.

properties.name: sessionId
properties.doc: A value to be used to create a sticky session, which can help getting more consistent results. As long as the same sessionId is used, a best-effort attempt will be made to target the same replica set. Be wary that reusing the same sessionID values repeatedly can interfere with the load balancing of the requests across replicas and adversely affect the performance of the search service. The value used as sessionId cannot start with a '_' character.

properties.name: scoringParameters
properties.doc: The list of parameter values to be used in scoring functions (for example, referencePointParameter) using the format name-values. For example, if the scoring profile defines a function with a parameter called 'mylocation' the parameter string would be "mylocation--122.2,44.8" (without the quotes).

properties.name: top
properties.doc: The number of search results to retrieve. This can be used in conjunction with $skip to implement client-side paging of search results. You can change this property as needed if you want to rotate your encryption key; Your data will be unaffected. Encryption with customer-managed keys is not available for free search services, and is only available for paid services created on or after January 1, 2019.

models.name: SearchIndex
models.doc: Represents a search index definition, which describes the fields and search behavior of an index.

properties.name: name
properties.doc: The name of the index.

properties.name: description
properties.doc: The description of the index.

properties.name: fields
properties.doc: The fields of the index.

valueType.name: SearchField
valueType.doc: Represents a field in an index definition, which describes the name, data type, and search behavior of a field.

properties.name: name
properties.doc: The name of the field, which must be unique within the fields collection of the index or parent field.

properties.name: type
properties.doc: The data type of the field.

properties.name: key
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field uniquely identifies documents in the index. Exactly one top-level field in each index must be chosen as the key field and it must be of type Edm.String. Key fields can be used to look up documents directly and update or delete specific documents. Default is false for simple fields and null for complex fields.

properties.name: retrievable
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field can be returned in a search result. You can disable this option if you want to use a field (for example, margin) as a filter, sorting, or scoring mechanism but do not want the field to be visible to the end user. This property must be true for key fields, and it must be null for complex fields. This property can be changed on existing fields. Enabling this property does not cause any increase in index storage requirements. Default is true for simple fields, false for vector fields, and null for complex fields.

properties.name: stored
properties.doc: An immutable value indicating whether the field will be persisted separately on disk to be returned in a search result. You can disable this option if you don't plan to return the field contents in a search response to save on storage overhead. This can only be set during index creation and only for vector fields. This property cannot be changed for existing fields or set as false for new fields. If this property is set as false, the property 'retrievable' must also be set to false. This property must be true or unset for key fields, for new fields, and for non-vector fields, and it must be null for complex fields. Disabling this property will reduce index storage requirements. The default is true for vector fields.

properties.name: searchable
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field is full-text searchable. This means it will undergo analysis such as word-breaking during indexing. If you set a searchable field to a value like "sunny day", internally it will be split into the individual tokens "sunny" and "day". This enables full-text searches for these terms. Fields of type Edm.String or Collection(Edm.String) are searchable by default. This property must be false for simple fields of other non-string data types, and it must be null for complex fields. Note: searchable fields consume extra space in your index to accommodate additional tokenized versions of the field value for full-text searches. If you want to save space in your index and you don't need a field to be included in searches, set searchable to false.

properties.name: filterable
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to enable the field to be referenced in $filter queries. filterable differs from searchable in how strings are handled. Fields of type Edm.String or Collection(Edm.String) that are filterable do not undergo word-breaking, so comparisons are for exact matches only. For example, if you set such a field f to "sunny day", $filter=f eq 'sunny' will find no matches, but $filter=f eq 'sunny day' will. This property must be null for complex fields. Default is true for simple fields and null for complex fields.

properties.name: sortable
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to enable the field to be referenced in $orderby expressions. By default, the search engine sorts results by score, but in many experiences users will want to sort by fields in the documents. A simple field can be sortable only if it is single-valued (it has a single value in the scope of the parent document). Simple collection fields cannot be sortable, since they are multi-valued. Simple sub-fields of complex collections are also multi-valued, and therefore cannot be sortable. This is true whether it's an immediate parent field, or an ancestor field, that's the complex collection. Complex fields cannot be sortable and the sortable property must be null for such fields. The default for sortable is true for single-valued simple fields, false for multi-valued simple fields, and null for complex fields.

properties.name: facetable
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to enable the field to be referenced in facet queries. Typically used in a presentation of search results that includes hit count by category (for example, search for digital cameras and see hits by brand, by megapixels, by price, and so on). This property must be null for complex fields. Fields of type Edm.GeographyPoint or Collection(Edm.GeographyPoint) cannot be facetable. Default is true for all other simple fields.

properties.name: permissionFilter
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field should be used as a permission filter.

properties.name: sensitivityLabelId
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field should be used for sensitivity label ID filtering. This enables document-level filtering based on Microsoft Purview sensitivity label IDs.

properties.name: sensitivityLabelName
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field contains the name of a Microsoft Purview sensitivity label applied to the document.

properties.name: sourceDocumentId
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field contains the source document identifier used for Purview audit tracking.

properties.name: sharepointSiteUrl
properties.doc: A value indicating whether the field contains a SharePoint site URL used for SharePoint group-based filtering.

properties.name: analyzerName
properties.doc: The name of the analyzer to use for the field. This option can be used only with searchable fields and it can't be set together with either searchAnalyzer or indexAnalyzer. Once the analyzer is chosen, it cannot be changed for the field. Must be null for complex fields.

properties.name: searchAnalyzerName
properties.doc: The name of the analyzer used at search time for the field. This option can be used only with searchable fields. It must be set together with indexAnalyzer and it cannot be set together with the analyzer option. This property cannot be set to the name of a language analyzer; use the analyzer property instead if you need a language analyzer. This analyzer can be updated on an existing field. Must be null for complex fields.

properties.name: indexAnalyzerName
properties.doc: The name of the analyzer used at indexing time for the field. This option can be used only with searchable fields. It must be set together with searchAnalyzer and it cannot be set together with the analyzer option.  This property cannot be set to the name of a language analyzer; use the analyzer property instead if you need a language analyzer. Once the analyzer is chosen, it cannot be changed for the field. Must be null for complex fields.

properties.name: normalizerName
properties.doc: The name of the normalizer to use for the field. This option can be used only with fields with filterable, sortable, or facetable enabled. Once the normalizer is chosen, it cannot be changed for the field. Must be null for complex fields.

properties.name: vectorSearchDimensions
properties.doc: The dimensionality of the vector field.

properties.name: vectorSearchProfileName
properties.doc: The name of the vector search profile that specifies the algorithm and vectorizer to use when searching the vector field.

properties.name: vectorEncodingFormat
properties.doc: The encoding format to interpret the field contents.

properties.name: synonymMapNames
properties.doc: A list of the names of synonym maps to associate with this field. This option can be used only with searchable fields. Currently only one synonym map per field is supported. Assigning a synonym map to a field ensures that query terms targeting that field are expanded at query-time using the rules in the synonym map. This attribute can be changed on existing fields. Must be null or an empty collection for complex fields.

freshness.name: FreshnessScoringFunction

type.name: FreshnessScoringParameters

properties.name: boostingDuration

properties.name: type
properties.doc: Indicates the type of function to use. Valid values include magnitude, freshness, distance, and tag. The function type must be lower case.

magnitude.name: MagnitudeScoringFunction
magnitude.doc: Defines a function that boosts scores based on the magnitude of a numeric field.

properties.name: parameters
properties.doc: Parameter values for the magnitude scoring function.

type.name: MagnitudeScoringParameters
type.doc: Provides parameter values to a magnitude scoring function.

properties.name: boostingRangeStart
properties.doc: The field value at which boosting starts.

properties.name: boostingRangeEnd
properties.doc: The field value at which boosting ends.

properties.name: shouldBoostBeyondRangeByConstant
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to apply a constant boost for field values beyond the range end value; default is false.

properties.name: type
properties.doc: Indicates the type of function to use. Valid values include magnitude, freshness, distance, and tag. The function type must be lower case.

tag.name: TagScoringFunction
tag.doc: Defines a function that boosts scores of documents with string values matching a given list of tags.

properties.name: parameters
properties.doc: Parameter values for the tag scoring function.

type.name: TagScoringParameters
type.doc: Provides parameter values to a tag scoring function.

properties.name: tagsParameter

properties.name: type
properties.doc: Indicates the type of function to use. Valid values include magnitude, freshness, distance, and tag. The function type must be lower case.

properties.name: functionAggregation
properties.doc: A value indicating how the results of individual scoring functions should be combined. Defaults to "Sum". Ignored if there are no scoring functions.

properties.name: defaultScoringProfile
properties.doc: The name of the scoring profile to use if none is specified in the query. If this property is not set and no scoring profile is specified in the query, then default scoring (tf-idf) will be used.

properties.name: corsOptions

type.name: CorsOptions
type.doc: Defines options to control Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) for an index.

properties.name: allowedOrigins
properties.doc: The list of origins from which JavaScript code will be granted access to your index. Can contain a list of hosts of the form {protocol}://{fully-qualified-domain-name}[:{port#}], or a single '*' to allow all origins (not recommended).

properties.name: maxAgeInSeconds
properties.doc: The duration for which browsers should cache CORS preflight responses. Defaults to 5 minutes.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.CustomAnalyzer.name: CustomAnalyzer
#Microsoft.Azure.Search.CustomAnalyzer.doc: Allows you to take control over the process of converting text into indexable/searchable tokens. It's a user-defined configuration consisting of a single predefined tokenizer and one or more filters. The tokenizer is responsible for breaking text into tokens, and the filters for modifying tokens emitted by the tokenizer.

properties.name: tokenizerName
properties.doc: The name of the tokenizer to use to divide continuous text into a sequence of tokens, such as breaking a sentence into words.

properties.name: tokenFilters
properties.doc: A list of token filters used to filter out or modify the tokens generated by a tokenizer. For example, you can specify a lowercase filter that converts all characters to lowercase. The filters are run in the order in which they are listed.

properties.name: charFilters
properties.doc: A list of character filters used to prepare input text before it is processed by the tokenizer. For instance, they can replace certain characters or symbols. The filters are run in the order in which they are listed.

properties.name: odataType
properties.doc: A URI fragment specifying the type of analyzer.

properties.name: stopwords

properties.name: odataType

properties.doc: A predefined list of stopwords to use. This property and the stopwords property cannot both be set. Default is English.

properties.name: ignoreCase
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to ignore case. If true, all words are converted to lower case first. Default is false.

properties.name: removeTrailingStopWords
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to ignore the last search term if it's a stop word. Default is true.

properties.name: odataType
properties.doc: A URI fragment specifying the type of token filter.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.SynonymTokenFilt.name: SynonymTokenFilter
#Microsoft.Azure.Search.SynonymTokenFilt.doc: Matches single or multi-word synonyms in a token stream. This token filter is implemented using Apache Lucene.

properties.name: synonyms
properties.doc: A list of synonyms in following one of two formats: 1. incredible, unbelievable, fabulous => amazing - all terms on the left side of => symbol will be replaced with all terms on its right side; 2. incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing - comma separated list of equivalent words. Set the expand option to change how this list is interpreted.

properties.name: ignoreCase
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to case-fold input for matching. Default is false.

properties.name: expand
properties.doc: A value indicating whether all words in the list of synonyms (if => notation is not used) will map to one another. If true, all words in the list of synonyms (if => notation is not used) will map to one another. The following list: incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing is equivalent to: incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing => incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing. If false, the following list: incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing will be equivalent to: incredible, unbelievable, fabulous, amazing => incredible. Default is true.

properties.name: odataType

properties.doc: The length at which terms will be truncated. Default and maximum is 300.

properties.name: odataType
properties.doc: A URI fragment specifying the type of token filter.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.UniqueTokenFilte.doc: Filters out tokens with same text as the previous token. This token filter is implemented using Apache Lucene.

properties.name: onlyOnSamePosition
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to remove duplicates only at the same position. Default is false.

properties.name: odataType
properties.doc: A URI fragment specifying the type of token filter.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.WordDelimiterTok.doc: Splits words into subwords and performs optional transformations on subword groups. This token filter is implemented using Apache Lucene.

properties.name: generateWordParts

properties.name: catenateWords
properties.doc: A value indicating whether maximum runs of word parts will be catenated. For example, if this is set to true, "Azure-Search" becomes "AzureSearch". Default is false.

properties.name: catenateNumbers
properties.doc: A value indicating whether maximum runs of number parts will be catenated. For example, if this is set to true, "1-2" becomes "12". Default is false.

properties.name: catenateAll

properties.name: splitOnCaseChange
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to split words on caseChange. For example, if this is set to true, "AzureSearch" becomes "Azure" "Search". Default is true.

properties.name: preserveOriginal
properties.doc: A value indicating whether original words will be preserved and added to the subword list. Default is false.

properties.name: splitOnNumerics
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to split on numbers. For example, if this is set to true, "Azure1Search" becomes "Azure" "1" "Search". Default is true.

properties.name: stemEnglishPossessive
properties.doc: A value indicating whether to remove trailing "'s" for each subword. Default is true.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.MappingCharFilte.doc: A character filter that applies mappings defined with the mappings option. Matching is greedy (longest pattern matching at a given point wins). Replacement is allowed to be the empty string. This character filter is implemented using Apache Lucene.

properties.name: mappings
properties.doc: A list of mappings of the following format: "a=>b" (all occurrences of the character "a" will be replaced with character "b").

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.PatternReplaceCh.doc: A character filter that replaces characters in the input string. It uses a regular expression to identify character sequences to preserve and a replacement pattern to identify characters to replace. For example, given the input text "aa bb aa bb", pattern "(aa)\\s+(bb)", and replacement "$1#$2", the result would be "aa#bb aa#bb". This character filter is implemented using Apache Lucene.

properties.name: tokenFilters

properties.doc: A description of an encryption key that you create in Azure Key Vault. This key is used to provide an additional level of encryption-at-rest for your data when you want full assurance that no one, not even Microsoft, can decrypt your data. Once you have encrypted your data, it will always remain encrypted. The search service will ignore attempts to set this property to null. You can change this property as needed if you want to rotate your encryption key; Your data will be unaffected. Encryption with customer-managed keys is not available for free search services, and is only available for paid services created on or after January 1, 2019.

properties.doc: The type of similarity algorithm to be used when scoring and ranking the documents matching a search query. The similarity algorithm can only be defined at index creation time and cannot be modified on existing indexes. If null, the ClassicSimilarity algorithm is used.

type.name: SimilarityAlgorithm
type.doc: Base type for similarity algorithms. Similarity algorithms are used to calculate scores that tie queries to documents. The higher the score, the more relevant the document is to that specific query. Those scores are used to rank the search results.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.ClassicSimilarit.name: ClassicSimilarity
#Microsoft.Azure.Search.ClassicSimilarit.doc: Legacy similarity algorithm which uses the Lucene TFIDFSimilarity implementation of TF-IDF. This variation of TF-IDF introduces static document length normalization as well as coordinating factors that penalize documents that only partially match the searched queries.

properties.name: odataType
properties.doc: The discriminator for derived types.

#Microsoft.Azure.Search.BM25Similarity.name: BM25Similarity
#Microsoft.Azure.Search.BM25Similarity.doc: Ranking function based on the Okapi BM25 similarity algorithm. BM25 is a TF-IDF-like algorithm that includes length normalization (controlled by the 'b' parameter) as well as term frequency saturation (controlled by the 'k1' parameter).

properties.name: k1
properties.doc: This property controls the scaling function between the term frequency of each matching terms and the final relevance score of a document-query pair. By default, a value of 1.2 is used. A value of 0.0 means the score does not scale with an increase in term frequency.

properties.name: b
properties.doc: This property controls how the length of a document affects the relevance score. By default, a value of 0.75 is used. A value of 0.0 means no length normalization is applied, while a value of 1.0 means the score is fully normalized by the length of the document.

Fog is essentially a cloud lying on the ground. Like all clouds, it forms when the air reaches its dew point—the temperature at  

which an air mass is cool enough for its water vapor to condense into liquid droplets.

This false-color image shows valley fog, which is common in the Pacific Northwest of North America. On clear winter nights, the 

ground and overlying air cool off rapidly, especially at high elevations. Cold air is denser than warm air, and it sinks down into the 

valleys. The moist air in the valleys gets chilled to its dew point, and fog forms. If undisturbed by winds, such fog may persist for 

days. The Terra satellite captured this image of foggy valleys northeast of Vancouver in February 2010.
